query: Which method can be used for concurrent strength–ductility improvement, and why?

generation.hypothesis: The introduction of a specific type of precipitate can lead to concurrent strength–ductility improvement in certain alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: Aluminum alloy 2024 in the T6 condition
generation.intervention: Aging treatment at 160°C for 12 hours to form a uniform distribution of coherent Al3Sc precipitates
generation.conditions: Aging treatment is conducted in an inert atmosphere to prevent oxidation
generation.mechanism: The coherent precipitates act as obstacles to dislocation movement, thereby increasing strength, while the uniform distribution of precipitates maintains a high level of ductility
generation.predicted_outcome: A 20% increase in yield strength and a 15% increase in elongation at break compared to the baseline
generation.baseline: Aluminum alloy 2024 in the T6 condition without aging treatment
generation.boundary: The improvement in strength and ductility is expected to occur within a narrow range of precipitate sizes and distributions
generation.uncertainty: The actual outcome may depend on factors such as the initial microstructure of the alloy, the precise aging conditions, and the resulting precipitate size and distribution

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing of aged and unaged samples
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the yield strength of the aged sample is not at least 10% higher than the baseline, or if the elongation at break is not at least 5% higher than the baseline, then the hypothesis is falsified
